To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the crossover operator of a direct encoding of trees, the edge-set encoding, without heuristics has no bias, (2) the crossover operator with the edge-set encoding using heuristics is bias towards the simple MST, (3) the bias of the heuristic crossover operator is not a problem for GAs using the edge-set encoding if the optimal solution to the problem is very similar to a simple MST.

the edge-set crossover is unbiased, that the crossover operator with heuristic is biased towards the MST, and that a GA using the edge-set encoding is able to find the global optimum only if the optimal solution resembles the MST.

the edge-set representation without heuristics has an unbiased crossover operator, that means it generates trees that are not biased towards particular types of trees, and that the crossover operator with heuristic is biased towards simple MST-like trees.
